title: Receptor binding domain of SARS CoV2 spike protein exhibits in vitro liquid-liquid phase separation due to structural disorderedness that may challenge the vaccine-generated antibody binding.
authors: Sodasani, Manikanta; Grandhi, Abhinav V K S; Mukala, Niharikha; Chintalapati, Jahnavi; Vissapragada, Madhuri; Aggunna, Madhumita; Yedidi, Ravikiran S
journal: Biochimica et biophysica acta. General subjects
one_liner_zh: 该文通过实验与分子动力学模拟揭示SARS-CoV-2刺突蛋白RBD的无序区域驱动体外液-液相分离，并可能影响抗体结合表位，虽非典型PPI建模，但聚焦IDR-LLPS机制且含物理模拟，对本课题有直接启发。
abstract: In this study we expressed, purified and demonstrated the protein liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) formation by the receptor binding domain (RBD) of coronavirus spike protein in vitro. Our molecular dynamics simulations revealed multiple structurally disordered regions lacking secondary structural elements within RBD that exhibited high structural flexibility with deviations as high as 6 A over 500 ns in support of our in vitro findings. Additionally these disordered regions overlap with epitopes potentially altering their architecture. Based on these results we conclude that the structural disorderedness of RBD causes LLPS formation in vitro and may potentially challenge the COVID-19 vaccine efficacy.
abstract_zh: 在本研究中，我们表达、纯化了冠状病毒刺突蛋白受体结合域（RBD），并在体外证明了其蛋白质液-液相分离（LLPS）的形成。我们的分子动力学模拟揭示了RBD内多个缺乏二级结构元件的结构无序区域，这些区域表现出高结构灵活性，在500纳秒内偏差高达6埃，支持了我们的体外发现。此外，这些无序区域与表位重叠，可能改变其结构。基于这些结果，我们得出结论，RBD的结构无序性导致体外LLPS形成，并可能对COVID-19疫苗效力构成潜在挑战。
